rows: A supercell crossed the El Paso/Hudspeth County line and continued to produce a swath of golf ball size hail, covering I-10 and leading to the overturning of a tractor trailer rig. No injuries were reported.
A microburst damaged a roof and caused some structural damage to a home in Dell City.
A tornado was observed by a sheriff's deputy near mile marker 114 on Interstate 10, about 6 miles southeast of Sierra Blanca.
Three-quarter inch hail was reported at I-10 and Acala Rd.
Golfball size hail was reported in Sierra Blanca.
Nickel to quarter size hail was reported at the United States Border Patrol Station in Sierra Blanca.
Several utility poles and trees were blown down in Dell City. A tin roof was also torn off of a house. In addition, rainfall totals of 1 to 2 inches were reported.

Power was knocked out in Dell City for more than 12 hours after wind blew the phase off of a transmission pole a mile and a half north of Highway 62/180. In addition 1 to 2 inches of rain also fell across the area.
A trained spotter reported a 20 foot diameter above ground pool which was not filled was blown over.
Hail was reported two miles west of Loma Linda.
Hail was carpeting the ground about 4 miles east-southeast of Loma Linda.
Trees and power lines down from near Esperanza to Fort Hancock. Barn blown down, tin roofing peeled from several barns and older buildings.
Storm survey estimated 80 mph winds occurred in Fort Hancock. There were some roofs blown off not so sound buildings as well as several trees knocked down.
Three tractor trailers and 1 horse trailer were overturned.
Lemon sized hail reported along with damaging winds.
Golf Ball sized hail was reported near mile marker 95 along Interstate 10.
Motorists encountered half dollar sized hail about 2 miles west of the U.S. Border Patrol check point.
Hail reported at the Cornudas Cafe. Hail fell for 10 minutes.

Hail from 1.5 inches to 2.5 inches in diameter was reported in and around Sierra Blanca. Some areas had hail up to 3 inches deep. Numerous house windows and automobile windshields were damaged, with many cars left dented. Hail also severely damaged dozens of roofs and even penetr…
Dell City mesonet recorded a peak gust of 72 mph.
The Sheriff reported downed power lines in Dell City.
A couple of mobile homes were destroyed by a microburst with winds estimated at 70+ mph.
Apparent microburst at the Dell City West Texas Mesonet Site.
Two weak landspout tornadoes were reported about 12 miles north of Sierra Blanca. Both lasted an unknown amount of time with no injuries or damage reported from them.
A Mesonet station recorded a gust of 58 mph. A trained spotter also reported damage across Dell City including a trampoline falling onto power lines and damage to the fire station.
The Dell City Mesonet site reported a peak gust of 61 mph.

A severe microburst occurred a couple miles northeast of Dell City. It was determined a collapsing thunderstorm moving south out of Otero County produced a severe microburst with wind speeds over 60 mph. The emergency manager reported wind damage with splintered power poles, flip…
The Dell City Mesonet site reported a peak gust of 66 mph with a thunderstorm in the area.
